title: Non-Derivative Use and Prompt Retention Commitment - Template
content:
Purpose:
This short template provides standardized language for customers and vendors when the parties require (a) a commitment that the vendor will not use customer prompts, prompt engineering, or output to train or improve foundation models (non-derivative use), and (b) clear retention and deletion mechanics for prompt data, including ephemeral scratchpads and telemetry. It is designed to be embedded as an addendum to a Master Services Agreement (MSA) or Data Processing Agreement (DPA).

Background and scope:
- Applies to all customer-provided prompts, instructions, example conversational history, and other text the customer submits to the vendor’s managed inference service (collectively, "Customer Prompt Data").
- Does not apply to anonymized, aggregated telemetry that cannot be reverse-engineered to recover prompt content, provided such telemetry is explicitly described below and permitted under Sections 4 and 5.

Definitions (short):
- "Non-Derivative Use": Using Customer Prompt Data in a way that does not create, update, or influence weights, parameters, or other trainable components of any model used or offered by the Vendor, nor using Customer Prompt Data to curate labeled training datasets for use in model training.
- "Prompt Retention Period": The time window the Vendor retains Customer Prompt Data in its systems, logs, ephemeral caches, or backups, before secure deletion.
- "Ephemeral Scratchpad": Temporary runtime buffers or in-memory caches used to service a single customer request or short-lived session.

Contractual Commitments (template clauses):
1) Non-Derivative Use Commitment:
Vendor shall not use, copy, or otherwise incorporate Customer Prompt Data into any process that trains, fine-tunes, or updates any machine learning models, model weights, or production model artifacts used by Vendor or its affiliates ("Non-Derivative Commitment"). For clarity, Vendor may use Customer Prompt Data to fulfill the immediate inference request and for debugging and support in accordance with Section 3, but shall not retain or use such data to improve or adapt Vendor-owned or Vendor-operated models.

2) Limited Use for Service Operations and Safety:
Notwithstanding Section 1, Vendor may use Customer Prompt Data for: (a) transient request routing, batching, and inference serving; (b) debugging, incident investigation, and remediation when Customer raises a support ticket or Vendor detects a service incident that reasonably requires access to prompt data; and (c) complying with legal obligations or responding to lawful requests, subject to the notice procedures in Section 7. Any use under this Section 2 shall be limited to the minimum data and personnel necessary and shall be governed by Vendor’s internal access control policies.

3) Prompt Retention and Deletion:
- Default Prompt Retention Period: Vendor will retain Customer Prompt Data for a default period of thirty (30) days unless a shorter retention period is configured by Customer via the Service controls or agreed in writing.
- Ephemeral Scratchpads: Ephemeral Scratchpads used solely to satisfy a single inference request will be cleared from memory immediately following completion of the request. Vendor will not persist Ephemeral Scratchpads to durable storage except in the explicit circumstances described in Section 2(b) (debugging & incident response).
- Backups and Archives: Vendor will implement procedures to ensure that Customer Prompt Data is excluded from long-term backups or, where exclusion is not technically feasible, that backups containing such data are retained only for the minimum time reasonably necessary and are deleted or securely isolated on a schedule no longer than ninety (90) days. Vendor will provide an attestation describing backup exclusion or retention cadence upon Customer request.

4) Allowed Aggregated Telemetry:
Vendor may collect aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry about service usage (e.g., average latency percentiles, token counts by anonymous buckets, queue lengths) for capacity planning and product analytics. Such telemetry must be processed in a manner that makes it infeasible to reconstruct Customer Prompt Data, and shall not be used to train or fine-tune models or create labeled datasets.

5) Explicit Opt-In for Model Improvement (optional):
Where Customer desires vendor to use Customer Prompt Data to generate improvements (model tuning, feature development), such use shall require explicit, written opt-in. The opt-in must: (a) identify the dataset or scope; (b) describe the intended use and retention; (c) provide mechanisms for Customer to revoke consent; and (d) include commercial terms and IP allocation for any derived improvements.

6) Access Controls, Personnel, and Audit Rights:
Vendor shall maintain documented access control policies that limit viewing of Customer Prompt Data to authorized personnel on a need-to-know basis. Vendor shall provide, upon reasonable request and subject to confidentiality obligations and redaction of unrelated data, a one-time audit report or summary of access logs for a specified retention window (not to exceed 12 months) demonstrating compliance with Sections 1–3. For frequency of audits above one per year, the Parties will negotiate scope and cost in good faith.

7) Incident Notification and Preservation of Evidence:
Vendor will notify Customer of any confirmed or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to Customer Prompt Data within seventy-two (72) hours of detection, provide an initial incident summary, and preserve relevant artifacts to support Customer’s forensic needs. Vendor shall not use preserved artifacts for model training and shall treat such artifacts as protected and governed by this Agreement.

8) Remedies and Injunctive Relief:
Violation of the Non-Derivative Commitment shall be considered a material breach. Customer may seek injunctive relief and damages, and Vendor agrees to cooperate with Customer in remediation including data deletion, forensic verification, and third-party audits at Vendor’s expense where material misuse is established.

9) Survival and Termination:
All obligations under this Addendum survive termination of the Master Services Agreement for a period of two (2) years, except obligations that by their nature should survive longer (e.g., data deletion attestations), which shall survive until performed.

Appendix A: Suggested operational checklist for engineering/ops teams:
- Offer a default "do-not-train" toggle in the Console and API (default = ON).
- Expose per-customer retention configuration (e.g., 0 days, 7 days, 30 days) with UI/ API enforcement.
- Implement strong deletion workflows: mark-for-delete, purge job, backup-stripping, and data-provenance logs.
- Maintain a short internal runbook for incident handling that maps to Clause 7 notification timelines.
- Provide a customer-facing attestation template for backup exclusion and deletion completion.

Notes for Negotiators / Commercial Teams:
- Customers sometimes accept a short opt-in window (e.g., 14–30 days) where vendor may retain prompts for feature development in exchange for credits or reduced price. Make opt-ins explicit and auditable.
- For regulated customers (healthcare, finance), prefer 0–7 day retention and stronger contractual audit terms.

References and linked materials:
- See Confluence page SEC-NonDeriv-2024 for background security controls and IAM mappings.
- Jira SEC-3421 contains engineering tasks for console toggle and retention APIs.
